name: Ur of the Chaldees
identification: Traditionally identified with Tell el-Muqayyar in southern Iraq. Some scholars propose a northern location.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Haran
identification: Harran, in south-eastern Turkey. Stephen calls it Charran (Acts 7:2).
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases
note: In Genesis 11:26–31 Haran is also the name of Abram’s brother. Only the place is marked.

name: Padan-aram
identification: The region around Haran in upper Mesopotamia.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Canaan
identification: The land west of the Jordan promised to Abram’s seed.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Shechem
identification: Tell Balata, beside modern Nablus. The KJV spells it Sichem in Genesis 12:6.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Beth-el
identification: Usually identified with Beitin, north of Jerusalem.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

samePlace.label: Luz
samePlace.phrase: the name of that city was called Luz at the first

samePlace.label: Luz
samePlace.phrase: Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Beth-el

name: Hai
identification: Hai (Ai) is often identified with et-Tell; the identification is debated.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Egypt
identification: Scripture names the land; the marker shows the Nile Delta only as a general location.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Hebron
identification: Hebron, in the hill country of Judah. Scripture places Mamre at Hebron (Genesis 13:18; 35:27).
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

samePlace.label: Mamre
samePlace.phrase: the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron

samePlace.label: Arbah
samePlace.phrase: the city of Arbah, which is Hebron

name: Moriah
identification: “The land of Moriah” (Genesis 22:2). 2 Chronicles 3:1 places “mount Moriah” at Jerusalem; Genesis does not say the two are the same place.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Beer-sheba
identification: Tel Be’er Sheva, in the Negev.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Dothan
identification: Tel Dothan, north of Shechem.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Goshen
identification: A region of the eastern Nile Delta; its exact extent is not known.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Rameses
identification: Usually identified with Pi-Ramesses at Qantir in the eastern Delta.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Succoth
identification: Often identified with Tell el-Maskhuta, east of the Delta. (A different Succoth appears in Genesis 33.)
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Etham
identification: “In the edge of the wilderness” (Exodus 13:20). The location is not known, so it is not placed on the map.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Rephidim
identification: The last camp before Sinai (Exodus 19:2). The location is not known, so it is not placed on the map.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Mount Sinai
identification: Traditionally Jebel Musa in the southern Sinai peninsula; other locations are proposed. Scripture also calls the mountain of the law Horeb (Deuteronomy 4:10; Malachi 4:4).
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

samePlace.label: Horeb
samePlace.phrase: the law of Moses my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb

name: Midian
identification: Land east of the Gulf of Aqaba; its limits are uncertain.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Moab
identification: The land east of the Dead Sea.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Bethlehem
identification: Modern Bethlehem, about 9 km south of Jerusalem.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Jerusalem
identification: Jerusalem, in the hill country of Judaea. David takes “the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David” (2 Samuel 5:7).
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Ramah
identification: Ramah of Benjamin, usually identified with er-Ram, about 8 km north of Jerusalem.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Ramah (Samuel’s home)
identification: Samuel’s home town (1 Samuel 1:19). Its location, and whether it is the Ramah of Jeremiah 31:15, is debated, so it is not placed on the map.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Babylon
identification: Babylon, on the Euphrates south of modern Baghdad.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Nazareth
identification: Modern Nazareth, in Lower Galilee.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Galilee
identification: The northern region west of the Sea of Galilee.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases

name: Judaea
identification: The southern region, including Jerusalem and Bethlehem.
source: Scripture references as cited; coordinates from standard biblical atlases
